confirm.description: Set up the discovered Rinnai water heater? It must already be bonded with this Home Assistant's Bluetooth adapter (see the README).

user.description: Select the Rinnai water heater to add.

abort.no_devices_found: No Rinnai heater found. Make sure a Bluetooth adapter is in range and the Rinnai app is closed.

init.description: Bonds are stored per adapter, so pin the adapter you paired the heater with if you have more than one. Keep the poll interval at 30 seconds or more for normal use. The minimum firing rate is from your model's data sheet (15,000 BTU/h for the RXP199iN); it sets the Low-Fire Margin. Fast polling reads the heater every 5 seconds while it is active, so short events such as false starts are caught; turn it off if your Bluetooth link struggles. On-demand link disconnects after every idle poll and holds the link only while the heater is running. The Rinnai app can then connect between polls.

data.fast_poll: Fast polling while the heater is active

experimental_write_k.name: Experimental \K write
experimental_write_k.description: Developer experiment, not a control feature. Sends the status query with exactly one byte changed, to find out whether the heater accepts commands on this register. See PROTOCOL.md section 8 before using it.

mode.name: Mode byte
mode.description: Value for byte 1. The heater reports 1 when idle and 2 while the recirculation pump runs. Give this or a setpoint, not both.

setpoint.name: Setpoint byte
setpoint.description: Value for byte 4 in °F. Use a setpoint below the current one for the first test. Give this or a mode, not both.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be on. This writes an unverified command to a gas appliance.

release_link.name: Release Bluetooth link
release_link.description: Disconnects from the heater and stays off it for a while. The heater accepts one Bluetooth connection at a time, so use this before opening the Rinnai app or when a technician needs to connect. When done, press Disconnect in the app or force-close it; in the background it keeps the connection.

reconnect.name: Reconnect now
reconnect.description: Ends a release or a reconnect wait and connects to the heater immediately.

bond_lost.title: Rinnai heater needs pairing again
bond_lost.description:
The heater at {address} keeps refusing this adapter's Bluetooth bond, even after asking for an encrypted link. This can happen after a new device was paired with the heater.

Turn on *Release Bluetooth Link*, then on the Home Assistant host run `bluetoothctl` interactively: `remove {address}`, `agent on`, `default-agent`, hold the heater's Bluetooth button until its LED is solid, then `pair {address}` and `trust {address}`, `disconnect {address}`, `quit`. Then press *Reconnect Now*; the first attempts can fail for about a minute. (The heater's Bluetooth LED is solid while a device is connected and off while the heater is free.) See *Bonding* in the README. This notice clears by itself once the heater answers again.
